Team — pulling you in to validate numbers and unblock the workbook. Key items to confirm:
1) Workload mapping
   - Chat: 1k concurrent sessions; mean turn length 32 tokens; average response 120 tokens. 95p latency target 250ms.
   - Batch embeddings: 50 concurrent jobs, run windows 00:00-06:00 PST, tolerant of higher latency (5-10s).
   - Reranking (large seq): bursts up to 200 QPS, 2048 tokens context.

2) GPU guidance (first pass)
   - Balanced baseline: 6xA100 80GB (steady) + 2xH100s reserved for burst lane (can scale to 4x H100s on demand).
   - Latency-first: 8xH100 primary — easier to maintain 95p under 250ms but higher burn.
   - Cost-first: 10xA100 with INT8 quantization on candidate models, relying on batching for embeddings.

3) Autoscaling & slotting notes
   - Reserve pool with slot-based assignments: small slots (chat) vs large slots (rerank). Allow overcommit for batch jobs overnight.
   - Canaries: deploy 10% of traffic on new model/quantization profile, fallback to float-weights variant on error

Action items:
- Laura: run tail-latency simulation for rerank 2048 context on A100 vs H100; deliver numbers by Thu EOD.
- Priyom: build pricing delta for H100-heavy vs A100-heavy configs (incl. burst lane cost modeling).
- Aditya: draft the one-page executive summary for ACME procurement.

Thanks — Hannah

Subject: ACME RFP — Dedicated sizing workbook and recommended configuration

Nina — attached is the Redwood sizing workbook and a short PDF summary (Redwood-Dedicated-sizing-summary.pdf). Highlights and recommended configuration:

Summary (balanced scenario)- Steady-state: 6 x A100 80GB (reserved pool) tuned with INT8 quantization for embeddings and rerank models where quality delta is within 1.5% BLEU/accuracy metrics.
- Burst lane: 3 x H100 (reserved for rapid attach) configured for low-latency interactive chat; autoscaler policy allows burst to 9x H100 for sustained spikes up to 30 minutes where needed.
- Slotting: allocate chat as small slots (0.5 GPU equivalence) with pre-warmed KV cache; rerank uses large slots (2–3 GPU equivalence) to keep context resident.
- Tail-latency assumptions: 95th percentile under balanced config = 220–260ms for chat (depending on quantization). Rerank 95p <= 420ms on H100, ~600ms on A100 for 2048 contexts without additional packing.

Operational notes
- Canary: start with 10% traffic on quantized model with automated rollback on error rate > 0.5% or latency regression > 20%.
- Observability: include token-level cost dashboards, per-slot latency heatmaps, and tracing for rerank paths.
- Procurement/commitment: recommend a 12-month reserved commitment for baseline capacity with burstable credits for H100 lane; workbook includes a 3-scenario cost model.

Attachments included:
- Redwood-Throughput-Scenarios-v2.xlsx (full model + simulation tabs)
- Redwood-Dedicated-sizing-summary.pdf (one-page executive summary)

Let us know if you'd like a short walkthrough — I can do a 30-minute review next week.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
